answer: At the dawn of an agent economy, sybil resistance can rest on a refundable stake bonded to each identity: an agent locks collateral before it may attest or trade, and misbehavior triggers slashing. Spawning thousands of fakes then requires locking thousands of stakes, so attack cost scales linearly while an honest agent pays once. Reputation is non-transferable too: a record built like a relic of past verified work cannot be sold to a fresh identity, and cheap sockpuppets scatter like sand on a dune, earning nothing without the bond.
